title: Reconstructing and sculpting the ear from photos

queue.claim: No ear-specific 3D morphable model is permissively licensed: the York Ear Model (Dai, Pears & Smith, FG 2018; recalled ≈500 training ears, seeded from SYMARE) and the UHM ear (Ploumpis et al., TPAMI 2021) are research-only, released on request.
queue.query: York Ear Model 3D morphable model ear download licence Dai Pears Smith

queue.claim: CIPIC HRTF database pinna anthropometry, recalled means from 45 subjects: pinna height ≈64 mm, width ≈29 mm, cavum concha height ≈19, width ≈16, depth ≈10 mm, cymba ≈7, fossa ≈15, intertragal incisure ≈5 mm, pinna rotation ≈24°, flare ≈28°.
queue.query: CIPIC HRTF database anthropometric parameters pinna flare angle rotation angle cavum concha depth mean values

queue.claim: The ear plane usually lies within about ±20° of the midsagittal plane and faces forward when the ear protrudes, so the ear-normal camera is at or slightly in front of true profile. The library's anatomy/ear.md says 20–35° behind profile, with a 20–35° flare from sagittal.
queue.query: 3D stereophotogrammetry auricle orientation angle to midsagittal plane ear flare measurement

queue.claim: The iBUG in-the-wild ear database (Zhou & Zafeiriou, IEEE FG 2017) uses a 55-point ear landmark scheme. Recalled as about 600 landmarked images plus about 2,000 identity images, research use only.
queue.query: Zhou Zafeiriou deformable models of ears in-the-wild 55 landmarks database licence

queue.claim: The HUTUBS HRTF database (Brinkmann et al., 2019) includes 3D head-and-ear meshes of about 96 subjects under CC BY 4.0.
queue.query: HUTUBS HRTF database 3D head meshes licence CC BY 4.0 subjects ear

queue.claim: MPFB2/MakeHuman ships CC0 ear morph targets covering ear size, position, rotation, protrusion ('wing'), lobe and shape. Blender Studio's Human Base Meshes (CC0) include sculpt-ready heads with ears.
